Daily work

Start the day knowing what matters.

Developers open one page and see their cards, their timer and the few things that need them. No hunting through boards.

My day

One page for the whole day

A personal home with your cards in priority order, what is overdue, blocked, failed in staging or waiting, today's meetings and anything unread.

  • Needs your attention lists only real problems, and says so when there are none.
  • Leads also see tickets waiting for review.
  • Security notice board sits right here, so global exposures are part of the morning routine.
Time

Honest time, almost no effort

Start your day, pick the cards you will work on, leave a note. End it the same way. Those notes feed each person's daily summary.

  • Timers start themselves when you move your own card to In Progress.
  • Finish-time countdown suggests how long a ticket should take from your own history for that story-point size, then counts down.
  • Late-start nudge: if nobody has started 30 minutes after work begins, a reminder goes out, unless it is leave or a holiday.
  • A 14-day grid shows hours worked per person, with leave and holidays marked.
Everywhere

Fast on a laptop, comfortable on a phone

The same workspace adapts to a phone with a bottom tab bar and a slide-in menu. Light, dark or follow-the-system theme, remembered per person.

  • ⌘K jumps to any page; g then a letter navigates; n creates a ticket; ? lists them all.
  • Cards work from the keyboard: Tab between them, m to move, Enter to open.
  • Board quick filters (My cards, Blocked, In review) are remembered between visits.
Delivery

Plan with the capacity you really have.

From backlog to production, with Jira staying the system of record and Dev Dashboard making it easier to use.

Board

A board that mirrors Jira, and respects the rules

Drag a card to the next stage. Cards only move forward, and developers can take their own cards up to Review while leads handle staging and production.

  • Your real Jira columns and statuses, mapped to the workflow once by an admin.
  • Blocked flag with a reason, shown on the card and in the sprint warning.
  • Live updates by Jira webhook, with a 30-second poll as a safety net.
  • Claude's first review of a linked pull request runs when a card enters Initial Review.
Sprints

Capacity that knows about leave

Fill a sprint from the backlog and see load against what each person can actually do, after approved leave and public holidays.

  • Auto-fill by priority until capacity is reached, with a buffer.
  • Per-person load bars warn when someone is over, and name who has room.
  • Forecast finish dates flag tickets likely to land late.
  • Start and close sprints, carry over work, create them in Jira too.
Estimates

Planning poker with a memory

The team votes in hours, reveals together, and sees a suggestion built from similar finished tickets.

  • Agreed estimates are written to Jira in the unit your project uses, story points or hours.
  • AI estimate review explains whether a number looks too low or high. Admins can always ask; others get it when their vote is far from the rest.
  • A spread check tells you when to discuss and re-vote.
Leave

Leave is part of the plan, not an afterthought

Request, approve and see leave on one calendar. Half days and several leave types are supported, and reasons stay private to the person, leads and admins.

  • Approved leave and public holidays reduce capacity, the expected progress line and every reminder.
  • Leave appears on Google Calendar for the team.
Insight

See how it is going, and why.

Numbers for leads, kind guidance for individuals, and the same facts presented for the people who ask.

Team overview

Progress by developer, at first sight

Each person's finished and in-flight tickets against where they should be today, adjusted for their leave.

  • Sprint health reads On track, At risk or Behind from done work against time used.
  • Pipeline bar shows every ticket status at once.
  • Burndown, recent activity and today's team status sit alongside.
Reports

Reports ready to present

Previous week, previous sprint or previous month, built from live data as slides.

  • Present full screen, print, or download PowerPoint and PDF.
  • Leads add a note to any slide before sharing.
  • Meeting engagement and code-review patterns are included, with per-person detail hidden from non-leads.
1:1 report

A monthly 1:1 that feels like a mentor wrote it

The last two weeks compared with the 30 days before, as a scorecard and a slideshow, with talking points for the conversation.

  • Encouraging by design: it opens with wins, frames growth areas kindly and ends on momentum.
  • Story points check asks whether a slow ticket was simply pointed too low for its scope.
  • Visible to the person, leads and admins only.
Quality

Find where bugs really come from

Dev Dashboard links bugs that appear in later sprints back to the earlier work they probably came from, using Jira links, ticket names, labels and wording.

  • Patterns, not blame: one or two bugs is normal. Only repeats across sprints or in one area are flagged.
  • One-click answers: whoever fixes a bug can confirm the cause, and that beats any guess.
  • AI judges each match and names the root cause: requirements, tests, review or code.
  • Export to PowerPoint or PDF.
People and analytics

Strengths, growth areas and trends

Each person's page shows delivery, estimates against reality by story-point size, and AI-written strengths and gaps across at least two sprints.

  • Estimate calibration shows whether work usually takes longer or shorter than estimated, to plan better.
  • Analytics cover team velocity, points and hours per developer, cycle time, where cards wait, estimate accuracy and meeting talk time.
  • Insights are visible only to the person, leads and admins.
Meetings

Meetings that leave something behind.

Record in the browser, get notes, decisions and action items, and turn them into work.

Notes

No bots joining your calls

Press Join and the recorder and steps appear straight away, even outside the scheduled time. Audio is transcribed with OpenAI or Gemini.

  • Automatic speaker tracking from a separate microphone stream, so quiet voices are counted properly.
  • AI notes: summary, decisions, risks, open questions and updates by person.
  • Create tickets for all action items as drafts, owners filled in where the name is clear.
  • Import Google Meet transcripts too. Only attendees and leads can edit a meeting's notes.
Decisions

Find out what was decided

Every decision from every meeting, grouped by month and searchable, with a link back to the meeting.

  • Meeting, sprint and monthly engagement reports show who takes part, with per-person talk time kept for leads.
AI, on your terms

Bring your own AI. Keep your own rules.

Use Claude, OpenAI or Gemini. Each person adds their own key in Settings, and it is stored encrypted. An admin can also provide a shared fallback.

What the AI does

  • Writes meeting notes and action items
  • Reviews estimates against similar work
  • Writes developer profiles
  • Writes the encouraging 1:1 report
  • Judges bug-origin matches
  • Explains security notices and fixes
  • Reviews pull requests (Claude)

How it stays trustworthy

  • Uses only your real data
  • Says when evidence is thin
  • Blame-free wording by instruction
  • Treats ticket text as data, never commands
  • Every result is labelled as AI, with the model
  • Rate limited, per person

Security notice board

  • Real advisories from GitHub and CISA
  • Exploited-in-the-wild flagged first
  • Filtered to your stack (Composer, npm and more)
  • AI explains what it means and how to fix it
  • One click to a backlog ticket
  • Leads alerted to new critical issues
Alerts and automation

Say the right thing once, to the right person.

Messages go by email, Discord and an in-app bell. Each kind is sent at most once a day per person, and never on leave or holidays.

Alerts

Helpful, not noisy

  • Overdue tickets and late-start reminders to the person.
  • Waiting tickets: a nudge after two working days in review or staging.
  • Sprint early warning to leads, with the reasons.
  • Sync failure alert to admins after an hour of trouble.
  • Email through ZeptoMail or Zoho Mail. Discord direct message or channel mention. Each person can switch channels off.
  • Jira auto-sync every 5 minutes, 08:30 to 17:30 on working days, plus webhooks for instant changes.
Security, privacy and control

Built so people can trust it.

Personal insight stays personal. Admins get the controls and the paper trail.

Access

Three roles, one clear rule

  • Sign in with email and password. New people request access and an admin approves them. Accounts lock after repeated failures.
  • Per-person data (insights, 1:1 reports, leave reasons) is visible to that person, leads and admins, never to peers.
  • Admins only see integrations, workspace settings and the audit log.
  • Admin changes are written to an audit log.
Admin

Set up in an afternoon

A step-by-step guide takes an admin through Jira, Google, GitHub, alerts and AI. After that the team runs itself.

  • Workspace timezone, working hours, holidays and meeting rhythm.
  • Jira people sync, status mapping, and duplicate merging.
  • Personal settings: profile photo, AI key, alert channels, password.

Why teams choose it

What changes on Monday.

Fewer status meetings

Progress, risk and blockers are visible and current. Leads ask better questions instead of collecting updates.

Plans that match reality

Capacity accounts for leave and holidays, and estimates learn from what actually happened.

A quality loop

Bugs link back to their origin, patterns surface early, and the fix goes into process, not into blame.

Privacy people can believe

Personal insight is private by design. Growth is framed kindly, with evidence and next steps.

Your tools, your AI

Jira, Google, GitHub, Discord and email stay as they are. Pick the AI provider and keep the key.

Less admin for everyone

Timers start themselves, meetings write their own notes, and reports build themselves.

Fits what you run

Integrations and hosting

Jira Cloud

OAuth connection, two-way sync, people import, estimates written back, webhooks.

Google Calendar and Meet

Meeting cadence, Meet links, leave on the calendar, transcript import.

GitHub

Pull requests linked to tickets, automatic Claude review, advisory feed for security.

Email and Discord

ZeptoMail or Zoho Mail. Discord bot messages or a channel webhook.

Claude, OpenAI, Gemini

One abstraction, your choice of provider and model, per person.

Hosting

Runs on Vercel with a Neon Postgres database. Releases deploy automatically from GitHub.
